chapter: Ch 7: Accounting Standards Based on Items Impacting Financial Statements
unit: Unit 4: AS 22 Accounting for Taxes on Income
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Overview and Core Definitions of AS 22
explain: AS 22 matches tax expense against accounting revenue of the period.
Accounting Income is the net profit or loss reported in P&L before tax expense or savings.
Taxable Income is the profit calculated under income tax laws to compute tax payable.
Tax Expense equals the total of Current Tax plus Deferred Tax charged or credited to P&L.
Current Tax is the tax payable or recoverable for the period based on tax laws.
Deferred Tax is the tax effect resulting from timing differences.

flow.title: Flow of Tax Expense Calculation
steps: Determine Accounting Income from P&L
Compute Taxable Income per Tax Laws
Calculate Current Tax Payable
Identify Tax Effect of Timing Differences
Calculate Total Tax Expense

topics.example: A business earns ₹6,00,000 accounting profit, but pays current tax of ₹12,000 on taxable profit. The tax effect of difference gives deferred tax of ₹1,08,000, making total tax expense ₹1,20,000.
remember: Current Tax + Deferred Tax = Tax Expense (Tax saving)
mistakes: Confusing current tax payable under tax law with total tax expense in financial statements.

quiz.q: What is the correct formula for Tax Expense under AS 22?
quiz.why: As per AS 22, Tax Expense is the aggregate of current tax and deferred tax charged or credited to P&L.

quiz.q: What is Deferred Tax under AS 22?
o: Tax paid in advance to tax authorities
The tax effect of timing differences
quiz.why: Deferred tax is defined specifically as the tax effect of timing differences between accounting and taxable income.

topics.title: Timing Differences vs Permanent Differences
explain: Timing differences originate in one period and reverse in one or more subsequent periods.
Example of timing difference: Machinery written off 100% for tax in year 1 but depreciated over life in accounts.
Permanent differences originate in one period and do NOT reverse subsequently.
Example of permanent difference: Fine paid for late payment of tax disallowed forever under tax laws.
Permanent differences increase or decrease current tax but NEVER result in deferred tax assets or liabilities.

flow.title: Classifying Differences between Accounting and Taxable Income
steps: Identify Difference in Income or Expense
Will the Difference Reverse in Future?
If YES: Classify as Timing Difference
Recognize Deferred Tax Asset or Liability
If NO: Classify as Permanent Difference
Do NOT Recognize Deferred Tax

topics.example: Fine paid to government is disallowed under tax laws permanently, creating a permanent difference with zero deferred tax impact.
remember: Only timing differences create deferred tax; permanent differences never do.
mistakes: Creating deferred tax assets or liabilities on permanent differences like tax fines or exempt incomes.

quiz.q: Which of the following differences results in the creation of Deferred Tax?
quiz.why: Deferred tax assets and liabilities arise strictly from timing differences that originate in one period and reverse later.

quiz.q: A fine paid for late tax submission disallowed under tax laws is an example of:
quiz.why: Fines disallowed permanently by tax laws do not reverse in subsequent periods, making them permanent differences.

topics.title: Recognition Principles & Prudence Rules
explain: Tax expense for current and deferred tax must be included in net profit or loss for the period.
Deferred Tax Assets (DTA) are recognized only when there is reasonable certainty of realization.
If an enterprise has unabsorbed depreciation or carry-forward tax losses, a stricter rule applies.
DTA on unabsorbed depreciation/losses requires VIRTUAL CERTAINTY supported by CONVINCING EVIDENCE.
Virtual certainty is a matter of fact supported by concrete evidence (e.g., binding profitable export order).
Mere profit projections, business plans, or restructuring proposals do NOT qualify as convincing evidence.

flow.title: Deciding Recognition of Deferred Tax Asset (DTA)
steps: Identify Timing Difference generating DTA
Check for Carry Forward Losses or Unabsorbed Depreciation
If NO: Check for Reasonable Certainty of Realization
If YES: Check for Virtual Certainty with Convincing Evidence
If Conditions Met: Recognize DTA in Books
If Conditions Not Met: Do NOT Recognize DTA

topics.example: A loss-making company holding a firm, un-cancellable export order guarantees future profit, establishing virtual certainty with convincing evidence to recognize DTA.
remember: Normal DTA needs reasonable certainty; Tax losses/unabsorbed depreciation need virtual certainty + convincing evidence.
mistakes: Recognizing DTA on tax losses based only on management's future budget projections without concrete evidence.

quiz.q: What level of certainty is required to recognize DTA when an enterprise has carry-forward tax losses?
o: Virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence
quiz.why: AS 22 states that carry-forward losses or unabsorbed depreciation require virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence.

quiz.q: Which of the following serves as convincing evidence for virtual certainty?
o: Future profit projections sent to a bank
quiz.why: Evidence must be concrete at the reporting date, such as a binding export order whose breach leads to heavy damages.

topics.title: Measurement, Re-assessment, and Review of DTA
explain: Current tax is measured using tax rates and laws applicable to the period.
Deferred tax is measured using tax rates and tax laws enacted or substantively enacted by balance sheet date.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities must NEVER be discounted to their present value.
At each balance sheet date, unrecognised DTAs are re-assessed and recognised if certainty criteria are met.
Carrying amount of DTA must be reviewed at every balance sheet date.
DTA is written down if realization is no longer reasonably or virtually certain; write-down can be reversed later.

flow.title: Measurement and Review Process of Deferred Tax
steps: Apply Enacted or Substantively Enacted Tax Rates
Do NOT Discount DTA/DTL to Present Value
Review Carrying Amount of DTA at Year-End
Is Realization Still Certain?
If NO: Write Down Carrying Amount of DTA
If Certainty Returns Later: Reverse Write-Down

topics.example: Deferred tax is calculated at 40% enacted rate. It is reported at full nominal amount without applying discounting for the 5 years it takes to reverse.
remember: Never discount Deferred Tax Assets or Liabilities to present value.
mistakes: Discounting deferred tax balances to present value because timing differences will reverse in long-term future.

quiz.q: Deferred tax assets and liabilities should be measured using:
o: Tax rates enacted or substantively enacted by balance sheet date
Average tax rate of the past 3 years
quiz.why: AS 22 specifies using tax rates and laws enacted or substantively enacted by the balance sheet date.

quiz.q: How should Deferred Tax Assets and Liabilities be presented regarding time value of money?
o: Discounted at government bond yield rate
Discounted only if timing difference exceeds 5 years
quiz.why: AS 22 explicitly states that deferred tax assets and liabilities should not be discounted to their present value.

topics.title: Presentation, Disclosure, and Offset Rules
explain: DTA and DTL must be disclosed under a separate heading in the Balance Sheet, distinct from current assets/liabilities.
Break-up of DTA and DTL into major components should be disclosed in notes to accounts.
If DTA is recognized for carry-forward losses/unabsorbed depreciation, nature of supporting evidence must be disclosed.
Current tax assets and liabilities can be offset ONLY if legally enforceable right exists and settlement is on net basis.
DTA and DTL can be offset ONLY if legally enforceable set-off right exists AND they relate to taxes levied by the same governing tax law.

flow.title: Rule for Offsetting DTA and DTL
steps: Identify DTA and DTL balances
Check Legal Right to Set Off Current Tax Assets/Liabilities
Are Taxes Levied by the Same Governing Tax Law?
If BOTH YES: Offset DTA and DTL on Balance Sheet
If ANY NO: Present DTA and DTL separately

topics.example: An Indian company offsets DTA and DTL originating under the Indian Income Tax Act because it has legal right and same tax jurisdiction.
remember: Offset DTA and DTL only if legally enforceable right exists and both relate to taxes under the SAME governing tax law.
mistakes: Classifying DTA or DTL under Current Assets or Current Liabilities on the face of the balance sheet.

quiz.q: Where should Deferred Tax Assets and Liabilities be presented on the Balance Sheet?
o: Under Current Assets and Current Liabilities
Under a separate heading, separated from current items
As a deduction from Reserves and Surplus
quiz.why: AS 22 mandates disclosing deferred tax under a separate heading, distinct from current assets and liabilities.

quiz.q: An enterprise can offset DTA and DTL only if they relate to taxes levied by:
o: Any tax law across the world
The same governing taxation laws with legal right of set-off
quiz.why: Offsetting requires a legally enforceable right and that both DTA and DTL relate to income taxes levied by the same tax law.

topics.title: Special Accounting Situations: Tax Holidays & MAT
explain: Tax Holidays (u/s 80-IA, 80-IB, 10A, 10B): Timing differences originating AND reversing WITHIN the tax holiday period are NOT recognized to the extent income is exempt.
Timing differences originating during tax holiday but reversing AFTER the tax holiday MUST be recognized in the originating year.
FIFO Rule: Timing differences originating first are assumed to reverse first.
Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT u/s 115JB): Tax paid under Sec 115JB is current tax for the period.
Deferred tax in MAT periods is measured using REGULAR tax rates, NOT MAT tax rates.

flow.title: Deferred Tax under Tax Holiday Assessment
steps: Identify Timing Difference during Tax Holiday
Determine Reversal Period using FIFO Rule
Does it Reverse WITHIN Tax Holiday?
If YES: Do NOT Recognize Deferred Tax
Does it Reverse AFTER Tax Holiday?
If YES: Recognize Deferred Tax using Regular Rate

topics.example: Out of 200 lakhs depreciation timing difference in year 1, 80 lakhs reverses inside tax holiday (not recognized) and 120 lakhs reverses after tax holiday (DTL recognized at regular tax rate of 40%).
remember: Always measure DTA/DTL using regular tax rates even when paying MAT u/s 115JB.
mistakes: Using the MAT rate (e.g., 7.5%) instead of regular tax rate (e.g., 20%) to measure deferred tax during MAT tax years.

quiz.q: Timing differences originating during tax holiday and reversing WITHIN the tax holiday period should be:
o: Recognized in full at regular rates
Not recognized to the extent total income is exempt
quiz.why: Timing differences originating and reversing inside tax holiday period are not recognized to the extent income is subject to tax holiday deduction.

quiz.q: When a company pays tax under MAT (Section 115JB), deferred tax assets and liabilities should be measured using:
o: Average of MAT rate and Regular tax rate
quiz.why: Relevant explanations state deferred tax must be measured using regular tax rates, not the tax rate under section 115JB.
